items.title: ADAMTS7 impairs endothelial angiogenic function via suppressing POSTN-mediated VEGFR2 activation in pre-eclampsia
items.author: Chao Wang
items.content: Angiogenic imbalance drives endothelial dysfunction in pre-eclampsia (PE). Here, the authors show the metalloprotease ADAMTS7 is elevated in the circulation of PE patients and impairs endothelial angiogenic function, suggesting the ADAMTS7/POSTN/VEGFR2 axis as a therapeutic target for PE.

items.title: Loss of confidence in commercial antibody validation threatens biomedical research integrity
items.author: Theam Soon Lim
items.content: Recent independent investigations conducted have identified thousands of apparently manipulated validation images across the online catalogues of more than a dozen commercial antibody suppliers. This points to a problem embedded in the antibody supply chain rather than at any single company. This represents a previously unaddressed entry point for unreliable data into biomedical research, upstream of the peer-review and image-integrity safeguards journals have put in place for manuscripts. This revelation has a profound impact on research data integrity and implications for data reproducibility across fields dependent on antibody specificity. This incident has put the spotlight on antibody suppliers to improve their processes to ensure properly validated products are being supplied to research labs.
